Whether you’re preparing for intimate dinners with friends or simply getting ready for a few more evenings spent curled up at home, the iconic homeware brand’s new-in range has everything your spaces could need.

items.key: ai:can a mushroom make music? devon exhibition explores 'cultural world' of fungi
items.text: Can a mushroom make music? Devon exhibition explores ‘cultural world’ of fungi
items.article: Exeter museum to host DJ’s ‘collaboration’ with woodland fungi and artist’s map of her own body’s mycobiome For one of the installations, a musician spent hours in woodland “collaborating” with fungi to create a soundscape inspired by the electricity they emit. Another is a kinetic sculpture of an extinct fungus that honours Beatrix Potter not for her tales of mischievous rabbits but for her lesser-known skills as a mycologist – a fungi expert. These are just two of the exhibits playing starring roles in a rather extraordinary contemporary art show called Living Labyrinths , at the Royal Albert Memorial Museum & Art Gallery (RAMM) in Exeter, aiming to celebrate the “cultural world” of fungi. Lara Goodband, the contemporary art curator at the RAMM, said it had been five years in the making. She suggested the south-west England was a good place to focus on fungi. “We have great weather for it, warm and damp,” Goodband said. “But also, I think people here have a special affinity for fungi.” She said a wide range of people in the south-west were fungi fans, from the ecologists who study the role they play in soil health to the ravers who enjoy the hallucinogenic properties of some mushrooms and the storytellers who work with the fairytale associations of toadstools.
